tool_args.rationale: All five observations are positive and lie at H = 0.16–0.48, far short of the forecast horizon of 21.8. The long-horizon probe directly tests whether the early sink-modulated gain persists or is overtaken by slow adaptation.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: At short horizons the slow term mainly constrains the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant, not the two parameters separately. A close pilot fit would not establish a reliable forecast at H = 21.8.
Finer trajectory measurements would help resolve fast transients, but would not directly test whether slow adaptation eventually offsets or reverses the early gain.
It can explain suppression at higher sink gradients but assumes away horizon dependence; the short pilot cannot validate that assumption.
